newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries weaken before retail sales, PPI data.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries weaken before retail sales, PPI data.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened lower on Wednesday just ahead of government reports on July retail sales and wholesale prices.

The Commerce Department's July retail sales report is expected to show that sales rose 0.7 percent in the first month of the third quarter and climbed 0.5 percent when auto transactions were excluded, according to a Reuters poll.
The Labor Department's Producer Price Index (PPI) is expected to show that wholesale prices rose 0.1 percent in July overall and 0.1 percent excluding food and energy.
Investors have been registering their nervousness about the retail sales report since Thursday and bond prices have fallen accordingly.
The report has become the focus of concern about an expected pickup in economic activity in the third quarter.
Consumer spending and economic growth tapered off in the second quarter after a brisk first quarter.

The question is whether an expected acceleration in consumer spending and economic growth in the third quarter will be moderate enough not to stir inflation fears. Investors hope to find a partial answer to that query in the sales data.
In June, retail sales rose 0.5 percent and were up 0.3 percent excluding auto transactions.
The June PPI was down -0.1 percent overall while the so-called core PPI, the index without its more volatile food and energy items, rose 0.1 percent.
Analysts also said revisions to previous months' figures are always a strong possibility for the retail sales data.
Minutes before the data were to be released, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 11/32 to 95-26/32, yielding 6.70 percent.
Three-month bill rates were up one basis point to 5.18 percent. Six-month rates were up two basis points to 5.25 percent. Year bill rates were up two basis points to 5.34 percent.
Two-year notes were down 1/32 to 99-23/32, yielding 6.03 percent. Five-year notes were down 2/32 to 98-29/32, yielding 6.26 percent. Ten-year notes were down 5/32 to 97-26/32, yielding 6.43 percent.
